CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for zuarrow.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md

What this is

zuarrow moves columns between R and the Apache Arrow columnar format: the C Data Interface in memory and the IPC stream and file formats on disk. It converts every Arrow type in the 1.x format to an R vector and back, reads and writes both IPC framings with LZ4 and zstd bodies, and keeps a registry that says which R class is the exact form of which Arrow type. The rule behind every conversion is exact or error: a value crosses without change or the call raises zuarrow_lossy_error naming the column and the exact target. The default is never warn or allow.

The one hard dependency is zukomp (Imports and LinkingTo), which supplies the IPC codecs. nanoarrow, arrow, DBI and duckdb are not dependencies at all, not even Suggests: they are test oracles that run in CI only (see Testing). The package is not a query engine, not Parquet, not a table object model, not transport (Flight, ADBC, PyCapsule) and not a replacement for nanoarrow: its handles are nanoarrow’s handles, so a session with both loaded passes objects between them without conversion.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0041 in pedrobtz/packages. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides. Its §13 decisions are all marked (C), the maintainer’s to overturn, and its §15 open questions are still open.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-09: every stage of .agents/roadmap.md, 0 to 11, is merged and its issue closed, Stage 11 (Review) on 2026-11-05. What remains is the CRAN-submission issue (#12).

The first critical review (2026-10-27, issues labelled review) has been fixed. Stage 10 wanted an upstream nanoarrow pull request for vendored patch 0004; that was not rechecked on 2026-11-09.

decimal’s registration (decimal#24) is optional. It is tested when decimal provides it, and 0.1.0 does not wait for it (design §12).

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is v0.1.0 (#1); submission is tracked in CRAN-submission (#12).

The design (§3) names zuint, decimal and zutempo as packages that register exact types with zuarrow at load, and zuggml, zuflow, zutable, qio and quak as consumers of its stream handles.

zuarrow itself waits on zukomp 0.2.0, the release that ships the lz4 and zstd codecs (zukomp#55); that release reaches CRAN first and sets the LinkingTo floor, which can happen 2026-11-27 at the earliest. Until then, verified 2026-11-09, DESCRIPTION builds on zukomp’s development version through Remotes: pedrobtz/zukomp, with zukomp (> 0.1.0) in Imports and LinkingTo. Once it is on CRAN, the first step of #12 is to remove Remotes: and set zukomp (>= 0.2.0).

Deviations from .claude/shared/workflow.md; this file wins for zuarrow:

  • The version stays at 0.0.0.9000 until submission (decided 2026-11-05), not 0.1.0 from Pre-flight. Setting 0.1.0 is a step of #12.
  • No cran-release.yaml yet. CRAN-SUBMISSION is still git-ignored, and a release is tagged by hand with pkg-post-cran: the bare version 0.1.0 (no v) on the submitted commit, the GitHub release, the bump to 0.1.0.9000, closing #1.

Commands

Beyond the shared devtools commands:

tools/update-vendor                              # re-vendor nanoarrow, rewrite PROVENANCE
tools/verify-vendor                              # vendored tree is upstream plus patches
tools/verify-vendor --canary                     # the verifier catches a missing patch
tools/run-benchmarks [--rows N] [--reps R]       # design §10 timings, as Markdown rows
tools/bench-types [--rows N] [--reps R]          # per-type conversion against nanoarrow
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "abi")'   # symbol checks (skip on CRAN)

tools/fetch-fixtures                             # arrow-testing corpus into tests/testthat/fixtures
Rscript tools/make-test-data.R                   # regenerate tests/testthat/data with arrow

Oracles 1 and 2 need the arrow-testing corpus. Fetch it with tools/fetch-fixtures, or set ZUARROW_FETCH_FIXTURES=true and the tests download it under tempdir(), as CI does; without either they skip. tests/testthat/data/ holds small files written by arrow and every input the fuzz target has crashed on, so those tests run everywhere.

Architecture

Design §4 names five layers. What exists so far:

  • Vendored nanoarrow in src/vendor/nanoarrow/ (see Vendored native code).

  • Handles in src/zar_xptr.c: owning external pointers in nanoarrow’s r.h layout, readers that accept any producer’s handles, the schema copy, printing, metadata, and the spec round trip. A spec is the R list list(format, name, flags, metadata, children, dictionary) that R/handles.R builds schemas from (zar_c_schema_from_spec) and reads them back into (zar_c_schema_to_spec).

  • Validation and comparison in src/zar_validate.c, plus a strict UTF-8 pass in src/zar_utf8.c, which nanoarrow’s full level lacks.

  • Internal constructors in src/zar_build.c: arrays from raw buffers, built without validation so tests can make malformed arrays, and a stream over arrays. Tests reach them through helper-arrays.R.

  • Conversion in src/zar_to_r.c (Arrow to R) and src/zar_from_r.c (R to Arrow). zar_c_to_r takes every batch at once: a plan per column picks the R form from the type and the lossy policy, a value scan settles the columns whose exactness depends on their values (int64 past 2^53, int32 INT_MIN, a NUL in a string), and each column is then allocated once and filled from every batch. R/to-r.R builds the data frame and raises the lossy conditions, naming the family package from zar_exact_target().

  • Nested conversion. A plan is a tree that mirrors the schema. A zar_slice reads a node’s elements in one batch, either directly or through a map (a dictionary’s indices, a run-end encoding’s runs), and up points at the enclosing struct, whose null rows make its fields NA. Factors take the union of every batch’s dictionary through a small hash table. Export takes list columns flattened by zar_prepare() in R, so C never calls R.

  • The registry lives in R/registry.R. Registered columns are converted in R: C leaves them (to code 9), zar_c_array_child() lends each batch’s field to the handler, and the pieces are combined with c(). A from handler’s array is moved into its slot only after the rest is finished, because nanoarrow’s finishing walks every child’s private_data as its own. A to handler takes two arguments, or three if it also wants the lossy policy. Its arity is checked at registration. Keys are tried in a fixed order: an extension name, then an exact format string, then a pattern (zar_handler_for()).

  • The IPC reader in src/zar_ipc_read.c holds the input in memory and walks the stream’s messages or the file’s footer blocks over nanoarrow’s decoder. Before decoding it verifies each header, checks every field node, buffer range, buffer alignment and compression prefix against arrow_limits() (zar_check_record_batch()), and copies a misaligned pre-0.15 message to aligned memory. Its core compiles without R under ZAR_STANDALONE for tools/fuzz/harness.c; src/zar_codecs.c is the zukomp adapter (a stub when standalone).

  • The IPC writer in src/zar_ipc_write.c encodes through ArrowIpcEncoderEncodeBatch(), which vendored patch 0013 adds: a record batch or a dictionary batch whose buffers go through zuarrow’s callback, 8-byte padded with zeros and compressed through zukomp. It writes the schema, each dictionary before the batch that first uses it, the batches, the end-of-stream marker, and for files the footer. test-write.R holds the MD5 of a fixed input in each format and codec, so a platform whose bytes differ fails.

  • Deferred strings in src/zar_altrep.c: with copy = FALSE, zar_build() turns a plain string or large_string column into an ALTREP STRSXP after the same per-value checks the copying fill makes. It keeps the batch handles in data1, caches each CHARSXP in data2 on first access, and drops the handles once every element exists. It has no serialization method, so saveRDS() writes a plain vector.

C never raises a condition. An entry point that fails frees what it owns and returns a zar_failure, list(kind, message). The R caller wraps every .Call() in zar_check(), which raises zuarrow_<kind>_error. Write the .Call() literally at the call site: R CMD check cannot see the registered routine through a variable.

Invariants that are easy to break

The design fixes these before any code exists; each has a consequence a test or CI leg will catch late. Add more as stages establish them.

  • zukomp is the only Imports (D2, D5). nanoarrow, arrow, DBI and duckdb are in no field of DESCRIPTION; bit64 and vctrs are never imported. Adding a dependency is a design change through the RFC, not a DESCRIPTION edit.
  • Handles use nanoarrow’s r.h layout (D6): malloc()ed struct, NULL release means unset, an array’s tag holds its schema, the protected field holds what keeps the memory alive. Deviating breaks interchange with DuckDB, Polars, ADBC, arrow and nanoarrow objects.
  • Class vectors are c("zuarrow_<kind>", "nanoarrow_<kind>") and S3 methods are defined on the first class only (D7). A method on the nanoarrow_* class overwrites nanoarrow’s when both packages are loaded.
  • lossy = "error" is the default everywhere, including the as.data.frame() and as.vector() S3 methods (D4, §15 Q4). A registration may make a lossy default exact and never an exact default lossy (§6.10).
  • Vendored nanoarrow builds with NANOARROW_NAMESPACE set to zuarrow and hidden visibility, so the shared object exports R_init_zuarrow only and no Arrow* symbol (§7, §9). Without it, loading nanoarrow in the same session clashes.
  • Conversion kernels never call back into R (§4). A column that needs a registered handler is left for the R-level dispatch; a kernel that calls R can longjmp over heap it owns.
  • Validate before allocating (§6.7): nothing goes on the R heap for an IPC message that fails validation, and every IPC input gets nanoarrow’s full level. The arrow-testing crash corpus is the regression set.
  • Little-endian only in v0.1.0 (D13): a big-endian schema is a zuarrow_format_error, not a silent misread.
  • Every crash input stays in the corpus. An input that the fuzz target or the crash corpus made fail goes into tests/testthat/data/ with its fix. The fuzzer then uses it as a seed, and the tests pin its outcome. A vendored fix is a numbered patch in tools/patches/, offered upstream.
  • Oracle packages stay out of the tarball. A test or helper that uses nanoarrow, arrow, DBI or duckdb goes in a test-ci-*.R or helper-ci-*.R file, which .Rbuildignore excludes, and guards with skip_without_oracle(). Anywhere else, R CMD check reports the use as an undeclared dependency. The oracles workflow runs those files with ZUARROW_ORACLES=true, where a missing oracle fails.

Testing

  • Shuffled runs rewrite snapshots. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) rewrites _snaps/*.md in the order the tests ran even when every snapshot matches (r-lib/testthat#2364). Discard a diff that only moves sections, git checkout -- tests/testthat/_snaps, and never commit one.
  • Conformance oracles. The design (§9) names four oracles: apache/arrow-testing‘s IPC golden files and crash corpus, fetched at a pinned commit into tests/testthat/fixtures/, plus nanoarrow and arrow for interchange. The golden files do not cover big-endian reading or the codecs’ own correctness.
  • Unreachable branches. tests/testthat/README.md records the C error branches no test can reach, and why.
  • Runtime. The whole suite took 15 s on 2026-11-04 with the fixtures fetched and every oracle installed: devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE), macOS x86_64, R 4.5.2. Under gctorture it runs a sample of the repeated loops (helper-gctorture.R).

Editing rules

  • Internal native symbols use the zar_ prefix (ZAR_ for macros), the prefix the design fixes in §3.
  • The one hard runtime dependency is zukomp, recorded as design D2.

Continuous integration

This package calls r-cmd-check.yml@v1 from .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml and coverage.yml (pinned to a commit) from .github/workflows/coverage.yaml; .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml is the r-lib/actions pkgdown workflow. .github/workflows/native-checks.yaml calls the sanitizers, valgrind, lto, rchk, analyzers and cran-special, and .github/workflows/gctorture.yaml calls gctorture. Its own and other callers:

  • oracles.yaml runs the *-ci-*.R tests from the source tree on Ubuntu with every oracle installed and ZUARROW_ORACLES=true. r-actions has no workflow that runs tests outside the tarball, hence one of its own.
  • fuzz.yaml fuzzes the IPC reader built without R (ZAR_STANDALONE): short runs on pull requests, a long run nightly, and a dispatch for the hour clean on the release candidate that design §12 wants: gh workflow run fuzz.yaml --ref <branch>. Its seed commit is kept in step with tests/testthat/fixtures-files.txt.
  • vendor.yaml re-derives src/vendor/nanoarrow with tools/verify-vendor and fails a pull request that changes the vendored files without src/vendor/PROVENANCE. vendor-upstream.yaml checks weekly for a new nanoarrow release.

The callers’ file names end in .yaml, so the full set is dispatched with gh workflow run R-CMD-check.yaml --ref main and gh workflow run native-checks.yaml --ref main; it also runs weekly on Monday.

gctorture: wide on every push, step 20 on a schedule

gctorture at step 20 is the most sensitive setting and by far the slowest job, so its job has GitHub’s six-hour limit (timeout-minutes: 360). It does not gate merges. Its own caller, .github/workflows/gctorture.yaml, copied from r-actions’ examples/gctorture.yml, runs it in two ways:

  • Every push and pull request runs the wide quick-step under a 10-minute budget (test-timeout-minutes). Past the budget the check fails red. Widen the step to get back under it; don’t skip tests to fit.
  • Step 20 runs on a schedule: daily while the roadmap is in active development, weekly once the package is released and changes slow down. Changing the cron line is the switch. A red scheduled run opens an issue labelled gctorture, and the next green run closes it. That issue is fixed like any other defect, before the next stage merges.
  • Dispatch step 20 on the branch before merging a change to PROTECTs, finalizers or external-pointer handles, and before Full CI, v0.1.0 readiness and the release commit: gh workflow run gctorture.yaml --ref <branch>. A green run on that commit is the evidence; a nightly run on another commit is not. That run is part of the definition of done for such a change.
  • Sample repetition, keep every path. gctorture finds an unprotected SEXP by running the path that holds it, not by running it again. Under gctorture, loops that repeat one path (fuzz iterations, property cases, the same input across versions) run a fixed sample. The caller sets an environment variable for it, ZUARROW_GCTORTURE=true, and helper-gctorture.R reads it. Every type, branch and error path still runs.

Vendored native code

The nanoarrow C library’s core and ipc components, Apache-2.0, release apache-arrow-nanoarrow-0.9.0 (commit 9fad802), live under src/vendor/nanoarrow/ (design §7, D1), with the flatcc runtime nanoarrow bundles. src/vendor/PROVENANCE holds the tag, commit, archive SHA-512, the SHA-256 of every file and the patch list; inst/COPYRIGHTS and LICENSE.note carry the notices, including three MIT and one BSD flatcc header. Its integration-testing header goes into the test harness only, never into zuarrow.so (D18). lz4 and zstd are not vendored; they come from zukomp (D2).

  • The tree is derived, never edited. tools/derive-vendor downloads the release, checks the SHA-512 Apache publishes, runs upstream’s ci/scripts/bundle.py --symbol-namespace=zuarrow --with-ipc --with-flatcc, splits the generated FlatBuffers code into nanoarrow_ipc_flatcc_generated.h and applies tools/patches/ in order. tools/update-vendor writes the tree and PROVENANCE; tools/verify-vendor re-derives and fails on any byte of difference, and --canary proves it would catch a missing patch.
  • Patches. src/vendor/PROVENANCE lists the series, 0001 to 0016, in the order applied. 0001-no-suppressing-pragmas removes flatcc’s #pragma diagnostic ignored lines (a NOTE); 0002-unused-locals fixes the two generated macros whose unused locals -Wall then reports (R CMD check counts “warning: unused” as significant). Every patched file carries a “Modified for the zuarrow R package” notice.
  • Visibility. src/Makevars defines NANOARROW_DLL empty, because nanoarrow otherwise marks its API visibility("default") and hidden visibility would not hide it. src/zuarrow-win.def exports R_init_zuarrow alone on Windows. test-abi.R checks both, and that nothing CRAN’s compiled-code check reports is referenced.
